candidates_considered.name: Solarworld Energy Solutions Ltd
candidates_considered.verdict: RESEARCHED and PUBLISHED (lane govt). Reg 30: WOS ZNShine Solarworld received a PO for 96,000 G12R 625 Wp panels at Rs 7,812.50 each = Rs 75.00 cr basic / Rs 78.75 cr incl 5% IGST. 96,000 x 625 Wp = 60.0 MW, so Rs 1.25 cr per MW - within 4% of the playbook's Rs 1.3 cr non-DCR module constant. The order itself is only 5.6-6.6% of a year's sales (the WEAKEST bucket the order study measured) and is not the reason to look. The reason is the BESS franchise behind it: three NTPC awards read field by field, 257 MW / 514 MWh for Rs 599.39 cr at Rs 1.08-1.19 cr per MWh, a sum the annual report independently confirms at Rs 5.99 bn - against GEC-III's Rs 50,000 cr for 50 GWh, an implied Rs 1.00 cr per MWh. Order book Rs 2,813 cr = 2.58x market cap; 8.2x trailing earnings, 1.29x book, at the 52-week low after -62.2% in a year. See ideas.json 2026-10-01-SOLARWORLD.

candidates_considered.name: Highway Infrastructure Ltd
candidates_considered.verdict: RESEARCHED, NOT PUBLISHED. Two orders read from the filings: a contract agreement for Gorakhpur Link Expressway toll collection from UPEIDA worth Rs 220,66,33,332 over 2 years (Rs 105,07,77,777 year one plus 10% escalation - arithmetic checks: 105.08 + 115.58 = 220.66), and an NHAI LOA of Rs 24,45,99,930 for the Velanchettiyur Fee Plaza, Tamil Nadu. Rs 220.66 cr against a Rs 321 cr market cap looks dramatic until you count the filings: HIGHWAY INFRASTRUCTURE FILED 35 ORDER-TYPE DISCLOSURES IN THE 760 DAYS TO 2026-10-01 (Moti Naroli, Katiyara, Venkatapalem, Kozhinjipatti, Palayam, Velanchettiyur...). Toll-plaza LOAs are its routine business, which puts it in the 8-or-more bucket the study found reached 2x only 17.3% of the time and 5x NEVER. Second problem: the filing never states which way the money flows on a user-fee collection contract - whether Rs 220.66 cr is revenue to the company or its remittance obligation to UPEIDA - so it cannot be sized against sales at all. Third: median 60-day turnover Rs 2.4 lakh, and only 1,423 shares traded on 2026-09-30. Not publishable.

govt_considered.release: Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme for Development of Intra-State Transmission System with Battery Energy Storage Systems (Cabinet, PRID 2316948, 30-Sep-2026)
govt_considered.verdict: KEPT AND WORKED - the one decision in this window whose money becomes somebody's order book. Rs 1,86,405 crore as parsed from the PIB release body by our own govt.py. Mapped to the 'transmission' basket (measured history: 47 companies, median 4.7x base-to-peak against 3.0x for the market, 49% made 5x) and to 'solar_kusum'. Two names researched and both published: JYOTI STRUCTURES (transmission tower + EPC, whose FY26 annual report names Green Energy Corridors AND BESS as its demand drivers, order book Rs 2,274 cr = 2.94x FY26 income, Q1 FY27 total income +57.1%, stock -41.0% over a year) and SOLARWORLD ENERGY SOLUTIONS (257 MW / 514 MWh of NTPC BESS EPC already won at Rs 1.08-1.19 cr per MWh against the Rs 1.00 cr per MWh GEC-III implies for its 50 GWh). CAVEAT ON THE SPLIT: pib.gov.in and pmindia.gov.in are both blocked from this sandbox, so the release body was NOT re-read. A web search of the official release gives Rs 1,36,378 cr for intra-State transmission, Rs 50,000 cr for 50 GWh of BESS, central support Rs 54,082 cr, target FY2032-33, 135 GW of RE evacuation - a search summary, not a document opened, and it does not reconcile exactly (1,36,378 + 50,000 = 1,86,378 against 1,86,405, a Rs 27 cr gap).

govt_considered.release: Cabinet approves Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28 (CCEA, PRID 2316941, 30-Sep-2026)
govt_considered.verdict: KEPT BY THE GATE, DISCARDED ON READING. Rs 8.36 lakh crore is the largest number in the window and it is the wrong KIND of number: farmer price support is a household/producer subsidy, which is the exact shape of PM Surya Ghar - the one basket in this repo's measured table that UNDERPERFORMED the market outright (1.8x against 2.0x). The question the playbook asks is not how big the number is but whose order book it lands in, and MSP lands in none. Also note the theme mapper tagged this release 'shipbuilding', a plain false positive, so its mapped company list is meaningless and was ignored.

govt_considered.release: Shri Chouhan Approves Rs 5,547.99 Crore Procurement of Pulses and Oilseeds Under PSS for Kharif 2026-27 (Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, PRID 2316939, 30-Sep-2026)
govt_considered.verdict: KEPT BY THE GATE, DISCARDED ON READING. Price-support procurement of agricultural commodities - again a producer subsidy, not an order book, and again mis-tagged 'shipbuilding' by the theme mapper. No listed small-cap beneficiary follows from it.

govt_considered.release: Cabinet approves One Network, Smarter Traffic: Delhi Moves to Real-Time Traffic Management (CCEA, PRID 2316953, 30-Sep-2026)
govt_considered.verdict: KEPT BY THE GATE, NOT RESEARCHED. Rs 1,789.52 crore for Delhi real-time traffic management IS a procurement that becomes somebody's order book - ITMS hardware, cameras, signal controllers, software integration - and it was mapped to 'defence' and 'shipbuilding', both false positives for this subject. The honest position: this release deserves research that the run's four-name budget did not allow, and the right basket for it (urban ITMS / surveillance electronics) does not exist in theme_map.json yet. Carried to the watch list rather than silently dropped.
